title: Work queues
summary: Move work off the request when the user does not need the result immediately.

parts.rule: A work queue holds jobs so a producer can acknowledge the user request before expensive work finishes. Consumers pull jobs, do the work, and often write results back to storage. The user path returns once the job is durably enqueued, not when the side effect completes.

body:
Rule. A work queue holds jobs so a producer can acknowledge the user request before expensive work finishes. Consumers pull jobs, do the work, and often write results back to storage. Decide delivery semantics (at-least-once is common), idempotency keys, retry limits, and a dead-letter path. The user path returns once the job is durably enqueued, not when the side effect completes.

Why it matters. Doing fanout, video transcode, or email inside the request thread blows latency and amplifies failures. Queues absorb spikes and isolate retries. Interviewers look for idempotency because at-least-once delivery will redeliver.

Worked example. Feed post write: API inserts the post row, enqueues FanoutJob{post_id=42, author=9}, returns 201 in twenty milliseconds. Workers pull jobs, load follower ids for author 9 (say fifty thousand), and append post 42 into each follower timeline table in batches. If a worker crashes after writing thirty thousand timelines, redelivery must not duplicate rows — use upsert on (follower_id, post_id). Email receipt after purchase: enqueue SendEmail; the checkout HTTP response does not wait on SMTP. Dead-letter after five failures for inspection. Contrast: password check on login stays synchronous — the user needs the answer now. Name the force before the mechanism. Name the force before the mechanism. Name the force before the mechanism. Name the force before the mechanism. Name the force before the mechanism.

[[diagram:queue-workers]]

When to use. Queue work the user does not block on: fanout, thumbnails, notifications, report generation. Use queues to smooth write spikes into steady consumer rates. Pair every consumer with an idempotent write.

When to refuse. Refuse a queue for the critical synchronous answer (authz, payment authorization). Refuse fire-and-forget without retries or dead letters. Refuse consumers that are not idempotent under at-least-once delivery. Refuse introducing a queue before the synchronous path is clear.
